children: Sanford's bull at Forsyth Barr shrugs off the prospect of lower profitability in FY27. That's because the New Zealand company had an exceptional squid season a year earlier, which will make it hard for FY27 wildcatch earnings to beat FY26. Analyst Paul Laxton Koraua also points to an unwinding of salmon biomass valuation gains in FY27 and further pressure on Sanford's mussels division. "However, cash generation should remain strong, supporting our forecast for a broadly net cash position by the end of FY27," Forsyth Barr says. It retains an "outperform" call on Sanford, noting its one-year forward price-to-earnings multiple of 11x represents an around 34% discount to the market median. Sanford is unchanged, at NZ$7.00, today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
